name: Limrun

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Public remote Xcode builds and streamed simulators with native automation APIs and log/video recording. Website advertises idle vs build-time rates but publishes no numbers on captured page; contact-sales. iOS simulator is not macOS desktop VM equivalence. Android also supported.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Billing model (from the official OpenAPI spec, no prices): subscription plans with monthlyPrice/yearlyPrice/minutePrice and included monthlyMinutes (credit-minutes that refill monthly). Usage is metered in credits on graduated tiers (labels like 'First 50,000' ... '5,000,001 and above'). Some plans have no overage ('overageRate ... absent when the plan has no overage'). Build instances are priced per phase (build, cache, sync, apiWork, idle); otherwise they are billed on wall-clock. Orgs carry concurrencyLimit and maxConcurrencyLimit. Terms: 'Limrun offers usage-based, monthly, and annual subscription plans. The fees, usage rates ... presented at checkout or set forth in an applicable order form will apply.'
Homepage advertises 'Idle/build time pricing' for remote Xcode (idle priced differently from build), with no numbers. /pricing returns 404, and Wayback has no pricing-page captures.

fleet.notes: Current mobile-dev cloud offering uses Book a Demo/contact workflow. Production-scale customer testimonials are not public self-serve quotas. New-account concurrent simulator/Mac limits, verification and turnaround unpublished.

snapshot_auto.quote: You can keep building on the same running instance without restoring again. The saved snapshot is for future instances and is only published when this instance terminates.
snapshot_auto.note: Xcode build sandboxes only, and opt-in: the instance must be created with --snapshot-key / spec.snapshot. Trigger: instance termination (delete, or the inactivity/hard timeout per the lifecycle docs); published only if the last build succeeded ("A failed compile or cancelled build does not produce a new snapshot"). Restore is automatic on the next create with the same key (prefix-matched restore keys, branch fallbacks). Disk/workspace only (sources + DerivedData), no memory. iOS simulators and Android emulators have no snapshot; only iOS keychain state can be saved/restored as an asset.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The saved snapshot is for future instances and is only published when this instance terminates.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No API/CLI to checkpoint a running instance; publication happens only at termination of a snapshot-configured Xcode sandbox (the closest thing: delete with --wait-snapshot). New Xcode sandboxes can restore from a key (effectively a warm template of disk state). No memory snapshots; nothing for simulators/emulators.

harness_api.quote: Install the `lim` CLI and the Limrun skills where your coding agent runs, then ask it for a product change.
harness_api.note: Agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) run outside Limrun and drive devices via the lim CLI, skills and MCP servers (remote https://mcp.limrun.com/mcp and per-instance mcpUrl). Limrun does not host or drive an agent harness inside its instances.

ingress_rules.quote: A `ready` instance carries the URLs its data plane needs in `status`. Every URL authenticates with the instance token, never the API key.
ingress_rules.note: Tokenized per-instance endpoints (apiUrl, mcpUrl, ADB WebSocket, targetHttpPortUrlPrefix for HTTP services on the device); separate stream-only token and signed stream URL (anyone holding it can watch and use the device); short-lived scoped tokens. No IP allowlists or private networking documented.

guest_firewall.quote: Everything runs with the permissions of the ADB shell user, so protected locations are rejected just as they would be for `adb`.
guest_firewall.note: Android emulators are non-rooted (docs also mention 'non-rooted devices' for Chrome flags); iOS simulators expose no shell. Xcode/Gradle build sandboxes run commands (lim xcode run) but root/network privileges are not documented. Not a general-purpose VM product.

secret_proxy.quote: Secret type; the registered types are enumerated below.
secret_proxy.note: The org secrets API only stores typed signing material (enum: androidSigningKey, appleCertificate, appleProvisioningProfile, appStoreConnectApiKey) used server-side by signing/upload builds; build env passed with --env. No credential-injecting outbound proxy. The 'Apple relay' (scoped token applerelay:*:connect) is a browser-to-Apple sign-in relay for store publishing, not a sandbox egress proxy.
